intro.text: These eight skills can be trained only with membership. They cannot be trained on free worlds, but the levels you have gained are kept. The route of stages 7–9 asks for little of them: Agility 25 for The Grand Tree (S7-04), Agility 40 and the Graceful pieces (S8-03), Slayer 18 for Animal Magnetism (S8-04). The plans below go further, up to level 99, and were checked against the OSRS Wiki training guides.

items.text: **Row codes** are the same as for the free skills: `AG-3` is Agility, the third row. The app highlights the row for your level.
**XP per hour** is taken from the wiki and assumes confident play. At first, while you are learning, it will be slower.
**Quests** often give several levels at once, so every skill has a list of them. Quests on the route are marked with a step code.

**Your level** is entered on the skill page; the plan row is highlighted by it. The route steps S7-04, S8-03 and S8-04 are ticked by the OSRS Path Bridge plugin itself once the required level is reached in the game.

intro.text: Agility is trained on courses: you go round a circuit of obstacles and get XP. With every level run energy recovers faster, and shortcuts (Agility shortcuts) open all over the world. Marks of Grace drop on the rooftops (Rooftop Agility Courses), and the light Graceful set is bought with them.

items.text: **The route:** 25 for The Grand Tree (S7-04), 40 and the first Graceful pieces (S8-03).
**Running:** the higher your Agility, the faster energy recovers. That speeds up everything else: quests, farming runs, trips to the bank.
**Shortcuts** around the world need various Agility levels. The World Map plugin in RuneLite labels their levels right on the world map.
**Members quests:** many need Agility, for example Cold War (30), Land of the Goblins (38) and Royal Trouble (40).

blocks.text: If your level is 20 above the course's requirement, five times fewer Marks of Grace drop. The exception is Canifis: the rule does not apply there, which is why Graceful is collected on it.

items.text: **The Grand Tree** (S7-05): 7,900 XP. From level 25 that is about 31 at once.
**The Tourist Trap**: two XP rewards of your choice. If you give both to Agility, you go from level 1 to 26: faster than running the first courses.
**Recruitment Drive**: 1,000, **The Depths of Despair** (needs Agility 18): 1,500.
Together these four quests give 19,700 XP, level 33.
The set is sold by Grace in the Rogues' Den, the basement of The Toad and Chicken pub in Burthorpe.
The price in marks: hood 35, top 55, legs 60, gloves 30, boots 40, cape 40. The whole set is 260 marks.
Every piece lowers weight and speeds up run energy recovery. The full set gives +30% recovery.
At Canifis from level 40 the whole set is collected in about 13–16 hours (500–900 laps). By then Agility will have grown to 54–59.
A mark lies on the ground for 10 minutes: pick it up at once. On free worlds Graceful does not lower weight.
**A Summer pie** raises Agility by 5: you can move on to the next course earlier.
**Food:** on the rooftops you sometimes fall and lose health. While your level is close to the course's requirement, keep a little food.
**Running without stops:** every rooftop obstacle restores 1–2% run energy, so you can run the course continuously.
**The official Agility world** is 346 (Members): there are more players on the courses.
**Less XP than in the plan?** The speed in the table is for play without mistakes and downtime. Falls and pauses lower it.
**Which course is best for Graceful?** Canifis, from level 40 to 60 and beyond: it has the most marks right up to the Ardougne course.
**Train Agility separately or along the way?** For the route 25 and 40 are enough. After that train when you want: running is faster and there are more shortcuts.

intro.text: Thieving is stealing from stalls (Steal-from), pickpocketing NPCs (Pickpocket), and picking locks and chests. The skill gives coins and useful items. A failed pickpocket stuns you for a few seconds and hurts your health, so keep food. Stealing from a stall is safe if the vendor and the guards do not see.

items.text: **The route:** the Fight Arena (S7-02) gives 2,175 Thieving XP, level 16 at once. The route does not ask you to train Thieving separately.
**Fairytale II** in full requires Thieving 40 (the route has only the start, S9-03).
**Money:** the Knights of Ardougne and stealing valuables in Varlamore bring coins along with XP.
**Members quests:** many require Thieving, for example The Feud (30) and Death to the Dorgeshuun (23).

Without big requirements: **Biohazard** (1,250), **Hazeel Cult** (1,500), **Tower of Life** (500), **Tribal Totem** (1,775, needs Thieving 21). Together with the Fight Arena that is 7,200 XP, level 24.
Further on: **The Queen of Thieves** (20): 2,000, **The Giant Dwarf** (14): 1,500, **Death to the Dorgeshuun** (23): 2,000, **The Feud** (30): 15,000.
**The Ardougne diary:** the medium tier gives +10% success to pickpocketing in Ardougne, the hard tier everywhere. You do not need to wear a pendant or cape, the bonus is permanent.
**The Dodgy necklace:** a 25% chance not to be stunned or take damage on a failure. It lasts 10 triggers.
**Gloves of silence** (Hunter 54): +5% success. The Ardougne diary bonus overrides them.
**The Rogue equipment** from the Rogues' Den minigame (from Thieving 50): the full set always gives double loot. XP does not increase.
**A guard attacked you after stealing from a stall?** The vendor or a guard saw you. Step away, wait until they lose interest, and steal so that you are out of sight.
**Too many pouches?** Without the Ardougne diary the inventory holds 28 pouches, with the medium one 56. Open them, or the thefts stop.
**Health melting away?** Take food or Dodgy necklaces. The higher the level, the rarer the failures.

intro.text: Slayer is combat by tasks. A Slayer Master gives you a task: kill a certain number of monsters of one kind. Slayer XP is awarded only for task monsters, roughly as much as the monster's health. Some monsters can be hit only with the required Slayer level, and against some you need a special item.

items.text: **The route:** 18 for Animal Magnetism (S8-04 to S8-05). The quest itself gives another 1,000 XP.
**Combat along the way:** a kill also gives ordinary Attack, Strength or Ranged XP.
**Slayer reward points:** they unlock the Slayer helmet, the Slayer ring and cancelling inconvenient tasks.
**Loot:** Slayer monsters drop valuable items, for example the Abyssal whip from the Abyssal demon (Slayer 85).

blocks.text: Take tasks from the strongest master your Combat level allows: their monsters give more XP per task.
They are sold by the Slayer masters (the Slayer Equipment shop):

items.text: **The Enchanted gem** shows how many monsters are left. The first one is given free with the first task, but only if you had no Slayer XP before. If you do the museum quiz first, you will have to buy the gem for 1 coin.
**Earmuffs** against Banshees (Slayer 15, the Slayer Tower in Morytania).
**A Bag of salt**: to finish off a Rockslug (20). **An Ice cooler**: to finish off Desert Lizards (22).
**A Mirror shield** against the Cockatrice (25).
**A light source**: in the Lumbridge Swamp Caves, where Cave bugs (7) and Cave slimes (17) live. Without light it is dark in the cave, and insects attack.
**Check your task:** right-click the master, Assignment, or use the gem in your inventory.
**Combat level counts:** by default the masters do not give monsters much stronger than you.
**Swapping a task:** Turael can swap another master's task for one of his own, an easier one, but the task streak resets, and the streak points with it.
**The monster takes no damage?** Then it needs a special item or a Slayer level.
**Why Slayer, if you can just hit monsters?** Some monsters cannot be hit at all without a task or the level. Besides, tasks give double XP: combat and Slayer.

**Who to take tasks from for S8-04?** From Mazchna in Canifis: there are more monsters in the task, and more XP too. Turael's tasks are short but give little XP: to get to 18 you will need many tasks.
**Expensive?** No: the items for the first tasks are cheap, and the main expense is food.

intro.text: Farming is planting in patches all around the world. Plants grow in real time, even when you are not in the game. XP comes from planting, checking the health of a grown tree and harvesting. The main method is tree runs: going round all the patches takes 5–10 minutes once or twice a day, and the rest of the time you train something else.

items.text: **The route:** Fairytale I (S9-02) gives 3,500 XP, level 17 at once.
**Fairytale II** in full requires Farming 49 (the route has only the start, S9-03).
**Herbs:** you grow herbs yourself for Herblore or to sell.
**Passive XP:** the trees grow by themselves: the best skill "in between".

**Tools:** a rake (Rake), a seed dibber (Seed dibber), a spade (Spade), a watering can (Watering can), a gardening trowel (Gardening trowel) for saplings. You can leave them with the Tool Leprechaun: he stands by every group of patches.
**A sapling** is made like this: a seed in a pot of soil (with a trowel in your inventory), water it from a can and wait. Saplings grow in the bank too.
**Compost** (Compost, Supercompost, Ultracompost) lowers the risk of disease and raises the yield.
**A gardener at a patch** for a fee (a basket of fruit, a sack of vegetables and so on) looks after the planting so it does not die. For a fee he will also chop down a grown tree.

blocks.text: Tree runs are the fastest way: if you do one or two a day, 99 comes in about 3–4 months. Saplings and the gardeners' fees cost money, so you need a source of income.

items.text: **Fairytale I - Growing Pains** (S9-02) — 3 500.

**Forgettable Tale...** (17): 5,000, **The Garden of Death** (20): 10,000, **Garden of Tranquillity** (25): 5,000, **My Arm's Big Adventure** (29): 5,000, **Enlightened Journey** (30): 3,000, the Recipe for Disaster subquest with the goblins: 1,000.
Together that is 32,500 XP, level 38.
Herbs grow in 80 minutes. Three herb patches are available at once: by Falador, Catherby and Ardougne. One more in Morytania after Priest in Peril.
Always put in ultracompost: the disease risk is lower and the yield is bigger.
The herb levels: guam 9, marrentill 14, tarromin 19, harralander 26, ranarr 32, toadflax 38, irit 44, avantoe 50, kwuarm 56, snapdragon 62, cadantine 67, lantadyme 73, dwarf weed 79, torstol 85.
A herb run is first of all earnings. The trees give more XP.
**The plant died?** It fell ill and you did not manage to cure it. Pay the gardener: then the planting will not die.
**Do you need to stand and wait?** No. You plant, leave, and come back when it has grown. The growth time runs without you.
**The Tithe Farm** in Hosidius (from Farming 34) is a minigame that gives the Farmer's outfit: it adds Farming XP.

intro.text: Herblore is brewing potions. A herb (Herb) and a vial of water (Vial of water) give an unfinished potion (Unfinished potion), to which a second ingredient is added. Potions boost combat and restore Prayer and run energy. The skill is almost entirely bought: XP comes from ingredients from the Grand Exchange.

items.text: **Combat potions:** Prayer potion (38), super attack, strength and defence, restoration (Super restore, 63).
**Run energy:** Energy potion (26), Super energy (52), Stamina potion (77).
**Fairytale II** in full requires Herblore 57.
The route does not require **Herblore**.

blocks.text: Without this quest Herblore cannot be trained at all.

items.text: The quest is started by Kaqemeex at the stone circle north of Taverley.
You need raw meat: bear meat (Raw bear meat), rat meat (Raw rat meat), beef (Raw beef) and chicken (Raw chicken). You dip the meat into the Cauldron of Thunder in Taverley Dungeon.
The reward is 250 XP, level 3 at once, and 4 quest points.

items.text: **Druidic Ritual** — 250.
**Jungle Potion** (3): 775, **Recruitment Drive**: 1,000, **The Dig Site** (10): 2,000. With Druidic Ritual that is level 19.
Further on: **Zogre Flesh Eaters** (8): 2,000, **Shades of Mort'ton** (15): 2,000, **Heroes' Quest** (25): 1,325, **Eadgar's Ruse** (31): 11,000.
**Grimy herbs (Grimy)** are cleaned first (Clean): that is XP too, slow but profitable.
**Vials of water, eye of newt and a pestle** are sold by Jatix in Taverley.
**The Amulet of chemistry** gives a chance to brew a 4-dose potion instead of a 3-dose one.
**Pouring potions** into 4 doses for free is done by Bob Barter by the Grand Exchange.
**Expensive?** Yes: Herblore is one of the most expensive skills. It is cheaper to brew what you will drink yourself, for example Prayer potions for combat.
**Where do I get herbs?** On the Grand Exchange or from your own patches (see "Farming").

intro.text: Hunter is catching animals and birds. Birds are caught with snares (Bird snare), butterflies with a net (Butterfly net), kebbits (Kebbit) with a noose (Noose wand), chinchompas with box traps (Box trap). The number of traps you can set at once grows with your level. In the Wilderness one extra trap is allowed.

items.text: **Chinchompas (Chinchompa)** are a ranged thrown weapon that hits several monsters at once.
**Gloves of silence** (Hunter 54) help Thieving.
**Members quests:** Eagles' Peak (27), At First Light (46) and others.
The route does not require **Hunter**.

items.text: **The Natural history quiz** (a miniquest in the Varrock Museum): 1,000.
**Eagles' Peak** (27) — 2 500, **The Ascent of Arceuus** (12) — 1 500, **Perilous Moons** (20) — 5 000.
**Bird houses** on Fossil Island (the quest Bone Voyage): passive XP, like patches: you set one up and collect it 50 minutes later.
**A Hunter potion** raises your Hunter level: you can catch new animals earlier and set an extra trap.
**The Ring of pursuit** shows the whole trail when tracking: less running around.
**The trap fell empty?** The animal escaped. With level there are fewer misses.
**How do I get to Piscatoris and the Feldip Hills?** Easiest by fairy rings (Fairy rings): they open with the start of Fairytale II (S9-03).

intro.text: Construction is furnishing your own house (Player-owned house): rooms, furniture, portals, an altar. XP comes from builds made of planks (Plank). The skill is expensive: planks are bought, and furniture is removed after building and built again. You need a saw (Saw) and a hammer (Hammer).

items.text: **The house as a teleport hub:** portals, a jewellery box, a restoration pool: at high levels the house replaces a heap of teleports.
**Members quests:** some require Construction, for example Cold War (34).
The route does not require **Construction**.

**The miniquest Daddy's Home:** start with Marlo in the estate agent's house in north-east Varrock. The reward: about 940 XP (level 8), a house in Rimmington and the crate Marlo's crate: 25 planks, 50 mithril nails, 10 oak planks, 5 steel bars, 8 bolts of cloth and teleports.
**Or buy a house** from the estate agent (Estate agent) for 1,000 coins.
**The house portal** stands in Rimmington. Right-click the portal, Build mode: you enter in building mode. From Magic 40 you can teleport to the house with the spell Teleport to House.

items.text: **Where do I get planks?** On the Grand Exchange. You can saw logs at a sawmill (Sawmill), but that gives no XP.
**Not enough level for a room?** Every room has its own level: the kitchen from 5, the dining room from 10, the workshop from 15.

intro.text: Fletching is making bows, arrows, bolts and darts from logs, feathers and tips. In the free version bows are only bought, and with membership you can make them yourself: for your own Ranged and to sell. You need a knife (Knife), sold in any General store.

items.text: **Your own bows and arrows** for Ranged.
**"On the go":** darts (Dart) and bolts are made in two clicks while you run an Agility course, do a quest or a farming run: XP at almost no cost in time.
**The route:** Animal Magnetism (S8-05) gives 1,000 XP, level 9 at once.

blocks.text: With a knife you get about 1,800 bows an hour, with a Fletching knife about 2,700. Stringing is faster than carving and gives as much XP. Bow strings are spun from flax (Flax) on a spinning wheel, which is Crafting from level 10.

items.text: **Animal Magnetism** (S8-05) — 1 000.
**Big Chompy Bird Hunting** (5): 262, **Zogre Flesh Eaters**: 2,000. Together with Animal Magnetism that is level 18.
**Temple of Ikov**: 8,000 and **The Fremennik Trials**: 2,812. With them it is level 30.
**Feathers** are sold by Gerrant's Fishy Business in Port Sarim, and they also drop from chickens.
**Darts** are the best way to train "on the go", but the tips (Dart tip) cost money.
**A bow for combat:** shortbows shoot faster, longbows farther. For training Ranged shortbows are usually taken.
**Where do I get logs?** Chop them yourself (see "Woodcutting") or buy them on the Grand Exchange.
**Is it worth it?** Stringing yew and magic bows usually pays for itself. Carving shafts from cheap logs is almost free.
